Q: @ not recognized by cobol z open editor WHY? A:

There is nothing wrong with your COBOL code (I have used the '@' character as an UNSTRING delimiter on the mainframe side with no problems) and it is not a character coding issue, either (since you have confirmed that UTF-8 is being used all around). But some characters can mean special things to an IDE or to a framework in which you are developing.

I don't use Visual Studio so I cannot advise you on that point. But I have had experience with various network developers complaining to me (where I am on the mainframe side) about using special characters in the userids and passwords I assign for them to be able to access mainframe APIs. Because of these characters, they cannot connect to the mainframe. When I remove the special characters, then their connections work just fine.

So, to prove this out... Try using a different delimiter (just for testing purposes). You can also see if your IDE or framework supports an escape character that you have to use in your delimiter literal.
